title: Foresight: Failure Detection for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation with Action-Conditioned World Model Latents

title: Fika Jobs raises $4M to build a video-first hiring platform where AI agents interview candidates
abstract: The hiring process has long been criticized for its inefficiency and opacity. Candidates spend hours writing applications and submitting cover letters, only to disappear into what often feels like a black box. Generative AI has only made things messier, with employers increasingly relying on AI-powered screening systems to sift through an overwhelming number of submissions. Stockholm-based startup Fika Jobs thinks there’s a better way. The company is building a video-first hiring platform that combines AI interview agents with short-form video profiles, creating something that feels like a cross between LinkedIn and TikTok. Instead of relying solely on resumes, candidates complete AI-powered interviews designed to showcase their personality and communication skills. Fika Jobs announced on Tuesday a $4 million pre-seed round, which will be used to continue developing the platform, grow the team, and prepare for a wider launch later this year. For job seekers, the process starts by connecting a LinkedIn profile. Fika’s AI reviews the candidate’s background and generates personalized interview questions. Candidates then complete a roughly 10-minute video interview with the AI agent, currently powered by Google’s Gemini models. After the interview, Fika automatically turns responses into short video clips and organizes them into a profile. Instead of applying to every new role, candidates maintain a live profile that employers can discover and revisit as new opportunities arise. Image Credits: Fika Jobs The idea came from co-founders and brothers Jakob Dubois (CEO) and Alexander Dubois (CTO) while they were building their previous startup. “When we were building [social app] Gaff, we spent a lot of time recruiting and almost passed on a candidate because his resume did not really stand out,” Jakob Dubois told TechCrunch. “We ended up speaking with him anyway, and within minutes, his grit, drive, and ambition became obvious. Exactly the kind of person we wanted to hire.”

title: The running list: major tech layoffs in 2026 where employers cited AI
abstract: Oracle disclosed Monday that it has reduced its workforce by 21,000 employees over the past 12 months, a decline of 13%, which means more cuts than was previously known, including because of AI. “The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce,” the company said in an annual financial regulatory filing . The revelation puts fresh numbers to what feels to many in the tech industry like an epidemic: companies reporting record revenues while simultaneously culling their workforces, pointing to AI as both the engine of growth and the reason for the cuts. Tech layoffs hit their highest single month in years in May, and AI was the most-cited reason, according to outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas. We recently wrote about why that rationale is something companies may want to rethink , not least because for many of these companies, the roles they’re now cutting ballooned during the pandemic hiring surge, raising questions about what’s really going on right now. Below is a running look — in reverse chronological order — at the bigger tech companies that have announced significant layoffs this year with AI as a stated factor. GitLab — June 3, 2026. In one of the most recent cuts on this list, GitLab laid off roughly 350 workers, about 14% of its staff , to fund AI infrastructure investment and handle surging traffic from AI workflows. CEO Bill Staples said agentic workloads are “pushing competitors to the brink” and that the company had begun a “generational rebuild” of its core infrastructure to support what he called 100x growth requirements. GitLab is exiting 22 countries, flattening management layers, and partnering with an unspecified AI lab to rebuild its platform for agent-scale workloads. The company reported first-quarter revenue of $264 million, up 23% year-over-year, and expects to incur $30 to $35 million in restructuring costs. Google — ongoing through May.

title: The AI world is getting ‘loopy’
abstract: On Friday, Claude Code creator Boris Cherny made an appearance at Meta’s @Scale conference and, surprisingly, the first question from the audience was about loops. “Are loops the next hype cycle,” the questioner asked, “or are they for real?” Cherny’s answer was an emphatic, “Yes, they’re for real.” “Two years ago, we wrote source code by hand. We started to transition so agents write the code. And now we’re transitioning to the point where agents are prompting agents that then write the code,” he continued. “As big as the step from source code to agents was, loops are just as important and as big a step.” Later in the talk (around the 32:00 mark in the YouTube video posted above), Cherny got specific about the loops he keeps running in his own work. One agent is continually looking for ways to improve the code architecture, while another looks for duplicated abstractions that can be unified. They submit pull requests like any other coder, and since the code is constantly changing, they never stop running. It’s a powerful idea, particularly with a figure as significant as Cherny behind it. With the shift to agentic AI, the focus for most users has been managing their agents as well as possible: establish clear goals, check in on discrete units of progress, and don’t let them stray too far beyond the prompt. The loop takes it a step further by authorizing a swarm of agents to work continuously in the background, endlessly. It’s a lot of trust to place in AI — but with models getting better fast, it could be the next step in getting AI to handle real work. The first thing to recognize is that this isn’t entirely new. Recursive loops — functions that call themselves in order to repeat an action, along with a condition that stops the loop — are a mainstay of intro computer science courses. abstract: Back to Articles Build real agentic apps using CUGA: two dozen working examples on a lightweight harness Enterprise Article Published June 23, 2026 Upvote 23 +17 Anupama Murthi anupamamurthi Follow ibm-research Hamid Adebayo harmedox Follow ibm-research Sami Marreed samimarreed Follow ibm-research Praveen praveenv Follow ibm-research Asaf Adi AsafAdi Follow ibm-research TL;DR — Building an agent is mostly plumbing: tools, state, guardrails, scaling from one agent to many. CUGA (pip install cuga), short for Configurable Generalist Agent, the Agent Harness for the Enterprise from IBM handles that, so you write just a tool list and a prompt. We built two-dozen single-file apps to prove it. Read one end to end here, then see how the same agent runs sovereign and governed in production without a rewrite. Most agentic apps start with a week of plumbing before the agent does anything useful. abstract: research area Data Science and Annotation , research area Speech and Natural Language Processing content type paper published June 2026 Metric-Dependent Annotation Saturation for Learning from Label Distributions Authors Guneet Kohli View publication Copy Bibtex When annotators disagree on a label, the disagreement itself carries signal—and the number of annotators needed to capture it depends on the evaluation metric. We fine-tune NLI models on label distributions subsampled from ChaosNLI, a dataset providing 100 independent annotator judgments per item, and identify metric-dependent saturation. In our 3-class NLI setting, entropy correlation—whether the model identifies which items elicit disagreement—requires N ≈ 20–50 annotators to converge, while distributional match (KL divergence) saturates by N ≈ 10 (87–95% of improvement across five model seeds). This finding rests on a prior observation: soft labels carry item-specific signal that label smoothing cannot replicate. Across five smoothing intensities, entropy correlation clusters at r ≈ 0.45–0.49, while soft labels reach r = 0.643 (p < 0.001); per-item analysis traces this gap to smoothing’s inability to distinguish ambiguous items from clear ones. The soft-label advantage replicates across two architectures (DeBERTa, RoBERTa), a non-NLI-pretrained baseline, and an exploratory cross-domain evaluation on content safety. These results suggest that annotation budgets should be informed by the target evaluation metric rather than set uniformly. Related readings and updates. title: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels
abstract: research area Data Science and Annotation , research area Speech and Natural Language Processing content type paper published June 2026 Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels Authors Guneet Kohli View publication Copy Bibtex LLM-as-a-judge panels aggregate votes from multiple models, with the expectation that diverse models yield more reliable evaluations. We develop a framework to measure the true informational value of such panels and quantify how far their reliability falls short of the independent-voting ideal. Testing a panel of 9 frontier LLMs from 7 model families on three natural language inference datasets (each with 100 human annotations per item), we find that the 9 judges effectively provide only about 2 independent votes’ worth of information. Roughly three-quarters of the panel’s nominal independence is lost because the models make the same mistakes on the same items. The consequences are stark: the panel’s actual accuracy falls 8–22 percentage points short of what independent voting would achieve, and the best single judge matches or outperforms the full panel across all conditions. Neither adding more judges nor using smarter aggregation algorithms helps — established methods close at most 11% of this gap, even with access to the correct answers. We quantify these findings using the Kish effective sample size (n_eff) and a Condorcet null model, and show the deficit is robust across prompt variants, temperatures, chain-of-thought reasoning, and a pairwise preference task (RewardBench). The bottleneck is correlated judges, not the aggregation algorithm, implying that scaling up panels cannot substitute for genuinely independent evaluation. Related readings and updates. 正行創新成立於2026年初，由連續創業者姚頌、著名跨國產業集團正大集團、清華知名青年學者於超聯合發起，以“用物理智慧給世界帶來便利”為使命，致力於探索物理智慧的技術邊界，通過世界動作模型與強化學習技術，推動將人形機器人大規模部署至真實商業與工業場景，目標成為全球可信賴的機器人服務提供商。 連續成功創業者與知名青年學者領銜，打造持續進化的全棧人才矩陣 title: 雲端計算一哥，讓小鵬、Kimi和獵豹都爽了一把
abstract: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 雲端計算一哥，讓小鵬、Kimi和獵豹都爽了一把 十三 2026-06-23 21:47:02 來源： 量子位 Agentic AI爆發的拐點已然來臨 金磊 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 有這麼一組資料，是真真兒地戳到了 用Agent 這件事的 爽點 。 來，展示： 公司AI程式碼覆蓋率超過70%； 內部已經建立700多個不同型別、不同部門的Skills； 連線400多個API端點；每天有100多個AI協同PR；累計跑完14萬多個工作流； 6個核心階段成功率均超過99.7%；交付程式碼0個P0、P1缺陷。 缺陷自動修復從兩天壓縮到10分鐘…… △圖片由AI生成 看完這些數字，想必大家腦海裡已經是一堆Agent塞滿一家公司的畫面了，而且是井井有條的那種。 這家率先嚐到Agent“甜蜜點”的公司是誰？ 小鵬汽車。 為什麼是它能做到？ 因為小鵬用了“雲端計算一哥”—— 亞馬遜雲科技 。 更準確地說，小鵬基於亞馬遜雲科技的 Kiro 、 Amazon Bedrock 、 Amazon EKS 等服務，搭了一套企業內部AI程式設計與Agentic工作平臺，名字叫 靈犀 。 小鵬集團AI/Data Platform負責人 何瑞邦 ，在 亞馬遜雲科技中國峰會 的現場講了一個非常具體的問題：2024年，小鵬內部已經普遍使用各種AI開發工具，一些員工的個人效率確實上來了，但整個部門的效率沒有明顯變化。 原因也很真實，一個稍微複雜點的專案，AI工具只能一環一環寫。寫完程式碼，還要人工整合、聯調測試、推CI/CD。 說得直白一點，就是程式碼寫得更快了，鏈路沒真正跑通。也正如亞馬遜全球副總裁、亞馬遜雲科技亞太區聯席總裁 儲瑞松 所說的： Agentic AI爆發的拐點已然來臨。AI Agent正在從一個輔助性工具，變成真正參與生產和價值創造的數字勞動力。 所以小鵬後來意識到一句話： 效率，不等於效能。 這其實也是很多企業用AI Coding、用Agent時的共同處境。單點提效很快，整體系統很慢；個人體驗很爽，組織收益不明顯。 小鵬的特殊之處在於，它面對的還不是普通軟體工程，而是更復雜的物理AI。 智慧汽車、Robotaxi、人形機器人、飛行汽車……這些場景裡，軟體和硬體綁得很緊。程式碼寫完之後，還要編譯、臺架驗證、迴歸、上線，鏈路更長，容錯率更低。 更關鍵的是，當AI生成程式碼的速度越來越快，人類review和治理的速度反而跟不上了。 這時候，小鵬選擇把AI Coding從寫程式碼工具，往前推進一步—— 讓Agent變成一支研發軍團。 一支永不下班的研發軍團 靈犀的架構，大致可以拆成五層。 最上面，是開發者入口，包括網頁端、IDE外掛和硬體開發外掛。開發者從這裡提出需求、管理任務、檢視結果。 往下一層，是Agent協作層。小鵬用Kiro做核心，把汽車行業的開發規範沉澱成Skills，讓一群Agent按規範協同作戰。 再往下，是資料和知識層。研發資料、專案上下文、Agent執行過程中學到的知識，都沉澱到這裡。 模型層，則由Amazon Bedrock提供大模型能力。 最底層是基礎設施。小鵬用Amazon EKS承載智慧體執行，需要多少算力，就彈性供給多少算力。 這套架構跑起來之後，結果就是開頭我們提到的那組數字：AI程式碼覆蓋率超過70%，700多個Skills，400多個API端點，14萬多個工作流，0個P0、P1缺陷。 其中最有代表性的變化，發生在SRE環節。 過去，一個缺陷自動修復可能要兩天。後來小鵬基於Amazon Bedrock，建立了四大SRE Agent和五維歸因，缺陷自動修復被壓縮到10分鐘。同類型bug下一次還能秒級命中，整個過程無需真人介入。 這也是Agent進入企業生產環境後，一個很典型的變化： 它帶來的不只是寫得快，而是把需求、設計、編碼、測試、部署、運維、治理這些環節連成閉環。 這和Kiro本身的定位也有關。 Kiro強調的是Spec驅動開發。也就是在真正生成程式碼之前，先把需求、設計、任務、測試都結構化，再讓Agent基於經過驗證的規範寫程式碼。 這樣做的目標很明確了，從源頭上提升正確性，而不是讓AI先猛寫，再把一堆技術債丟給人類收拾。 所以，小鵬這個案例最有價值的地方，在於它把企業研發體系裡的“上下文、規範、工具、模型、算力、治理”一起串了起來。 這才是Agent真正起作用的樣子。 大家可能常常聽到一種經典建議： 先拿幾家練練手，再把重要的公司集中到同一時間段，等offer一起來再談價格。 Alisa說，大方向沒錯，但這裡面有三個大坑。 1、練手有成本。 你不是超人。練得太多，等排到真正在意的公司時，人已經垮了。 2、時機這件事，不全由你掌控。 對方有沒有headcount、哪個team在招人——這些外部變數，有時候比你準備得多充分更關鍵。 abstract: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 可口可樂的世界盃TVC，居然是prompt生成的 聽雨 2026-06-23 14:10:04 來源： 量子位 24小時線上，2秒回話，陪你聊球 聽雨 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 什麼？這屆世界盃，能一邊看球一邊跟範指導嘮嗑了？！ 是的，開啟可口可樂中國小程式 “可口可樂吧” ，你可以隨時跟範指導嘮上兩句：上海口音原汁原味，熱梗張口就來，聊球照樣犀利。 更關鍵的是，從你說完到他回話， 不到2秒 ，而且全年無休， 24小時線上 。 這還只是開胃菜。 開幕式前，一支以范志毅為主角的10秒宣傳影片上線；整個世界盃週期，可口可樂還有一支限定版TVC，5人5城、導演級運鏡，全部由AI生成。 是的，過去千萬級預算才能拍出來的廣告大片， 這次是prompt生成的 。 操盤這一切的，是 可口可樂 和 百度一鏡 。百度一鏡的前身是 慧播星 ，上個月剛在百度Create大會上完成品牌升級。 那麼問題來了： 一個能以假亂真、還能即時接梗的范志毅，到底是怎麼捏出來的？ 世界盃上的范志毅數字人，是什麼體驗 世界盃上的范志毅數字人，和你印象裡那種放錄影式的虛擬形象，完全不是一個物種。 打個比方，傳統數字人是播片，范志毅數字人是現掛： 你可以隨時打斷他，他不會卡殼；你半天不說話，他會主動找話題把你撈回來；你實在不知道聊什麼，他還會遞上幾個推薦問題。 更細的地方在於，他能感知你的狀態，你今天情緒如何，他聽得出來。 對話中斷了也沒關係，能接著上次的話茬繼續聊，不會每次見面都像初次認識。 聊到興起，還能一句話給範指導即時換個背景，從演播室切到球場邊。對使用者來說是個彩蛋，對品牌來說則是多一個場景的自然曝光。 可口可樂的世界盃TVC ，創意概念也很巧妙：一罐世界盃限定可樂=社交重啟按鈕。 【此處無法插入影片，遺憾……可到量子位公眾號檢視～】 故事從一張限定版可樂照片開始，沉寂許久的群聊被點燃，許久沒聯絡的老友依次冒泡，每一條訊息背後，都是一段和世界盃有關的故事。 最令我驚奇的，是它的 一致性 。 5個人物、5座城市，運鏡風格高度統一，推拉搖移、機位排程、構圖層次全都線上。 導演、攝影、美術、剪輯、調色、聲音的完成度，也堪稱專業製片水準。 據瞭解，百度一鏡先對可口可樂做了深度品牌學習，把歷史TVC和人群分析都餵了進去。 所以成片不是泛泛的AI素材拼接，品牌調性一整個拿捏了。 不過呢，好玩只是表象，表象之下是一整套技術棧在託底。 能不能做到 快、像、穩三者兼得 ，才是即時互動數字人真正的分水嶺。 快、像、穩，闖過三關才算范志毅 先說 快 。 即時互動數字人從接收使用者資訊到完成反饋，端到端響應要控制在2秒以內。 單看數字可能沒感覺，但要知道，這2秒裡要完成的事情包括： 聽懂你說了什麼、識別你的情緒、組織一段符合范志毅人設的回答，再即時生成對應的語音、表情和動作，並且讓所有模態嚴絲合縫地對上。 單獨做到快不難，單獨做到細也不難，難的是同時做到。不少方案要麼犧牲時延換效果，要麼犧牲效果換時延，而百度一鏡把這個平衡做到了業內領先。 然後是 像 。 像分兩層。第一層是 形似 ：范志毅數字人的每一幀表情和動作，都是現場算出來的，不是預錄素材的迴圈播放。 依託百度自研視覺模型，它可以生成符合語義的複雜動作和指向性動作，長時間穩定可控，不卡頓、不變形、不出戲。甚至在商品互動場景裡，數字人拿起一罐可樂演示入口食用，全程穩定無形變。 第二層是 神似 ，這一層要難得多。 口音、方言、俚語要精準還原，足球專業知識要線上，熱梗要接得住，還得結合每日熱點即時輸出新內容。一個只會用標準普通話念稿的范志毅，觀眾一眼就能看穿。 有趣的靈魂，比好看的皮囊難造多了。 最後是 穩 ，也就是這一切背後的底層架構。 支撐范志毅數字人的，是 文心大模型 加上百度一鏡的 數字化群體智慧AI大腦 。 這個AI大腦具備深度思考、任務規劃與自主協同能力，能夠理解、拆解並推演複雜任務，再智慧排程多個專家智慧體分頭執行，從內容生成到互動決策全面自動化。 換句話說，你看到的是一個范志毅，背後其實是一整支團隊在打配合。 title: 機器人全棧作業系統！老黃率先丟擲“具身版安卓”
abstract: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 機器人全棧作業系統！老黃率先丟擲“具身版安卓” henry 2026-06-23 14:06:02 來源： 量子位 輝達：不造機器人，但要幫具身企業造好機器人 henry 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 輝達不造機器人，但要幫具身企業造好機器人（doge） 剛剛，在芝加哥Automate 2026大會上，輝達釋出了 Halos for Robotics —— 一套覆蓋晶片、感測器、作業系統到安全認證的全棧機器人安全系統。 Halos最大的特點，是把輝達過去在 自動駕駛領域 超過 18600工程人年 的安全積累和700萬行經過驗證的程式碼，搬到了 機器人賽道 ，為自主機器人提供統一的安全架構。 有了它，機器人公司不用再從零造輪子，接入即可使用。更關鍵的是，Halos的 核心安全框架已經開源 ，向行業開放。 可以說，如果 特斯拉 做具身智慧走的是 iOS 路線，自己造機器人、自己做安全，那麼 輝達 選的就是 安卓 路線，把安全平臺開放給所有人。 值得一提的是，目前已經有不少公司入夥Halos生態，成為首批合作伙伴，包括人形機器人公司 Agility 、波士頓動力、雷射雷達廠商 禾賽科技 、安全機器人公司 FORT Robotics 等，整體生態已經擴充套件到 43家 往上。 其中，Agility已經率先吃上“螃蟹”，將Halos整合進自家的Digit機器人，在亞馬遜、GXO、豐田的工廠裡持證上崗。 影片裡這個穿著安全背心的機器人，正穿梭在工廠傳送帶之間，承擔搬運和物流等實際工作。 從晶片到軟體，安全管三層 那這個新的安全系統Halos到底是個什麼東西？ 按照輝達官方的架構，Halos可以分成四層，從下到上分別是： 平臺安全 、 安全作業系統 、 演算法安全 和 生態安全 。 這四層其實對應的是同一個問題的四個維度—— 機器人在現實世界執行時，可能出錯的四個來源：硬體、軟體系統、模型決策，以及外部認證與生態。 首先是平臺安全，解決底層硬體不能失控 。 輝達在這一層拿出了IGX Thor，一顆面向機器人與工業場景的AI計算平臺。 它內部設定了一個獨立的“安全島”，擁有獨立的處理器、I/O、電源和時鐘，與主計算系統物理隔離。 即使主AI系統崩潰、重啟甚至異常執行，安全島仍然可以獨立執行緊急制動等關鍵功能。 這有點像飛機的備用系統，當主系統失效時，備用系統仍然能接管控制。 同一層還有 Holoscan Sensor Bridge ，用來解決另一個關鍵問題：感測器異構帶來的延遲與錯配。 機器人通常同時搭載雷射雷達、深度相機、IMU、力矩感測器等裝置，但這些裝置來自不同廠商、執行在不同協議上。 如果資料需要層層排隊處理，就可能在幾十毫秒內錯過安全視窗。 Sensor Bridge的作用，是把所有感測器資料統一接入安全計算域，實現低延遲同步處理，並達到SIL 2級安全保證。 第二層：安全作業系統，解決“系統本身會不會出錯” 如果說第一層管“硬體不崩”，這一層管的是“系統不亂”。 Halos OS執行在IGX Thor之上，底層是Halos Core，支援兩種模式：純Linux，或者Linux + QNX混合架構。 在後者中，輝達通過Hypervisor把系統拆成兩個隔離域：Linux負責AI計算與應用，QNX負責安全關鍵任務。兩者完全隔離執行。 這意味著即使AI應用層出現異常，也不會影響安全控制邏輯。這一層相當於在“硬體安全島”之外，再加一層“軟體隔離牆”。 在此之上，是安全應用模組，其中最典型的是Outside-In Safety Blueprint。 它的思路是：不只讓機器人自己看世界，還引入外部視角。 比如在工廠天花板安裝攝像頭，由獨立AI從第三方視角監控機器人行為。 在一個具體場景中，自主叉車在拖車內作業時，車載感測器容易誤判空間邊界，導致頻繁急停。 而Outside-In系統可以在確認環境安全時允許更高效率執行，一旦有人進入危險區域，再立即接管幹預。 這一能力目前已向開發者開放，並以開源形式提供。 第三層：演算法安全，解決“AI本身會不會判斷錯” 前兩層保證的是“系統可靠”，但機器人真正的風險，其實來自更上層——模型本身。 無論是VLA（視覺語言動作模型）還是VLM（視覺語言模型），它們的決策都可能出錯。 例如把紙箱誤判為人，或者把人誤判為障礙物。這類錯誤不是系統崩潰，而是“理解錯誤”。 演算法安全這一層的目標，就是評估並約束模型在物理世界中的行為安全性，確保錯誤不會轉化為危險動作。 第四

title: 馬斯克又盯上AI基建：特斯拉要賣“算力積木”了
abstract: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 馬斯克又盯上AI基建：特斯拉要賣“算力積木”了 聽雨 2026-06-23 14:02:11 來源： 量子位 新商標已曝光 聽雨 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 特斯拉也盯上AI基建生意了。 剛剛，特斯拉向美國專利商標局(USPTO)提交了一個名叫 “Megapod” 的商標申請，計劃銷售模組化AI資料中心硬體。 根據商標描述，這是一套用於AI計算的模組化資料中心硬體系統，裡面包括計算機伺服器、AI資料處理硬體、網路裝置、配電單元和冷卻系統。 但是，就在不到一年前，特斯拉才剛剛 解散了Dojo團隊 ，親手砍掉了自己唯一的自研AI訓練超算。 剛把Dojo送走，這會兒又給AI資料中心註冊新商標。 嗯？特斯拉這是換了個姿勢，繼續搞算力了？ Megapod是什麼 目前能確定的資訊來自商標申請。 特斯拉提交的商標名是MEGAPOD，申請序列號為99893717，申請日期是2026年6月18日。 型別上，這是一個標準字元商標，也就是先把“MEGAPOD”這個名字佔住。申請基礎是intent-to-use，意思是“有意使用”，但產品還沒有正式上市。 商標申請裡的描述則相當具體，檔案中寫到，Megapod覆蓋： 用於人工智慧計算的模組化資料中心硬體系統，包括計算機伺服器、用於人工智慧資料處理的計算機硬體、網路裝置、配電單元和冷卻系統。 還包括“自包含的模組化AI計算硬體系統”，以及“用於監控、管理和最佳化上述系統的可下載軟體”。 通俗來說，Megapod像是一個 即插即用的AI資料中心模組 。 一個機櫃裡，把伺服器、網路裝置、電源、散熱系統全塞好，拉到工地通上電，就能直接跑AI訓練和推理。 這也是它和特斯拉現有 Megapack 、 Megablock 一脈相承的地方。 Megapack賣的是大型儲能電池，Megablock是更大規模、更模組化的儲能系統。 而Megapod聽起來，則像是把“模組化”這套思路，從電力系統搬到了AI算力系統裡。 有網友因此直接喊出： 特斯拉悄悄展示了一項龐大的AI基礎設施佈局 。 還有人進一步聯想，這可能和馬斯克此前提到的“利用閒置電力跑AI”有關，甚至猜測特斯拉未來會不會把超充網路、電池儲能和AI計算節點連線起來，形成分散式AI基礎設施。 不過目前來看，Megapod還只是商標申請，既沒有樣機、沒有引數，也沒有價格，更沒有交付時間表。 因此離Megapod真正成為產品，還有很長一段路要走。 不過這個商標本身，也說明特斯拉已經在認真考慮， 把AI基礎設施變成一個可銷售的硬體品類 。 特斯拉要搶輝達的生意？ 乍一看，Megapod很容易讓人想到輝達。 畢竟現在AI資料中心裡最貴、最核心的東西，就是輝達的整櫃算力系統。 比如 GB200 NVL72 ，已經是當下高階AI資料中心的事實標準之一。 一個機櫃裡整合GPU、CPU、高速互聯、液冷和網路，客戶買走後直接部署大模型訓練和推理。現在全球雲廠商、AI公司、主權AI專案，基本都在圍著這套體系轉。 也就是說，在“模組化AI算力”這門生意裡，輝達已經是絕對核心玩家。 那麼特斯拉的Megapod，是不是要來搶輝達的飯碗呢？ 短期來看，倒也未必。 因為特斯拉自己也是輝達客戶。特斯拉訓練FSD、機器人和車端AI模型，需要大量GPU；馬斯克旗下的xAI，也在大規模採購輝達晶片建設訓練叢集。 不僅如此， 特斯拉自研AI晶片的歷史也是相當坎坷 。 特斯拉曾經高調押注 Dojo超算 ，希望用自研D1訓練晶片支撐FSD模型訓練。 2021年AI Day上，特斯拉正式展示Dojo和D1晶片，邏輯是通過自研訓練系統加速自動駕駛模型迭代。 但到了2025年，Dojo團隊被解散，負責人離職，部分成員流向AI晶片創業公司，剩餘人員轉崗到特斯拉其他資料中心和計算專案。 馬斯克隨後也表示，公司不應分散資源擴充套件兩套不同AI晶片設計，後續重點轉向AI5/AI6，並更多依賴輝達、AMD等外部算力生態。 由此看來，眼下特斯拉的新動作，未必是要搶輝達的GPU生意，更可能盯上的是AI資料中心的另一層生意： 電力、儲能、冷卻、配電和模組化部署 。 這也是AI資料中心目前的痛點所在。大模型訓練和推理正在瘋狂吃電，新的AI資料中心不只是缺GPU，也缺電網接入、缺變電容量、缺冷卻系統、缺可以快速部署的基礎設施。 很多專案晶片到了也不一定能開跑，往往還卡在供電、散熱、施工週期和併網審批上。 而這些問題，剛好更接近特斯拉能源業務的能力邊界。 特斯拉真正賺錢的AI生意，

title: 小扎「蒸餾員工」計劃緊急喊停！私聊資料都洩露了…
abstract: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> 小扎「蒸餾員工」計劃緊急喊停！私聊資料都洩露了… 魚羊 2026-06-23 08:33:00 來源： 量子位 Meta這團亂麻，幾頓零食是搞不定了 魚羊 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 難怪Meta CTO都不得不承認“內部士氣快跌到歷史谷底”了。 圍繞AI，小扎又整出了新的么蛾子： 之前不是說要把員工們全蒸餾了嗎？這事緊急叫停了， 因為資料搞！洩！露！啦！ 原本說是要記錄大家電腦上滑鼠移動、點選、鍵盤輸入等操作資料，來訓練AI。 結果把人傢俬聊記錄、績效資料弄得滿公司亂飛，直接一個2級事故（0-5級，0級最嚴重）。 Meta發言人已經證實了此事，還找補了一下： 我們在設計該專案時已仔細考慮過隱私保護措施。 雖然目前沒有跡象表明有員工不當訪問了這些資料，但我們仍決定在調查期間暫停該專案。 （我要是Meta員工，那確實……我謝謝你啊） “煉化”員工結果爆大雷 給大家從頭捋一捋事情的前因後果。 今年4月， 小扎急得跳牆 ，Meta發了個內部公告，說是為了 幫助Agent更好地理解人類如何使用電腦 ，要強制監控員工的滑鼠和鍵盤操作。 直白一點說就是要把員工的一舉一動都化作投餵AI的資料。員工不能say no的那種。 當然大廠嘛，說法上還是要講體面的。當時說的是，監控的具體範圍 僅限制在常用工作軟體 ，如Gmail、GChat、Metamate和VSCode，並且員工的手機是不會被監控的。 但知公司莫若員工啊，Meta內部一開始反對的聲音就挺激烈，其中很大一個原因就是擔心個人資料洩露。 果然，這才兩個月，出事了。 據Business Insider爆料，Meta內部已經緊急叫停了這個名為MCI（Model Capability Initiative）的專案，原因是 敏感資料被發現一度全員可見 。 這個敏感資料涉及 45000份 員工資料表，不僅有AI工具涉及的完整提示詞和轉錄文本，還包括員工私聊記錄、績效資料等等…… 這下，Meta內部又雙叒炸了。 CTO Andrew Bosworth不得不出來直面員工怒火，承認該專案執行過程中沒有達到隱私審查設定的標準，承諾後續會分享調查結果。 我們出現了ACL（訪問控制列表）配置錯誤，需要徹查原因，追蹤所有資料訪問記錄並進行分析。 有Meta員工向《連線》透露，目前此事件的狀態是“已結束”。 不知道問題解沒解決，反正Meta發言人說的是“資料沒有被不當訪問”。但也有訊息指出，在問題得到控制前，已經有數十名員工主動訪問了這些資料。 Meta士氣跌至谷底 前些天，Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth（Boz）剛在內部會議上承認，公司為了AI又是重組又是整活的，已經快讓“內部士氣跌到歷史谷底了”。 員工們不再相信自己的專長會被看見、相信自己能在Meta成長、相信自己的工作真的有影響力。 現在看來，這個谷底還不知道要低到多底。 Boz的應對策略是精簡併穩定組織架構，還恢復了一批被砍掉的福利，比如辦公室的微型茶水間、差旅預算、團建經費。 但目前看來，Meta這團亂麻，不是靠幾頓零食就能梳理清楚的。 參考連結： [1] Twenty GitHub issues cost 59 KB. One access log — 45 KB. After 30 minutes, 40% of your context is gone. title: Transfer Learning for Low-resource Genomic Mutation Detection
abstract: The detection of genomic mutations plays a central role in understanding cancer biology, enabling more precise diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic strategies. However, accurate mutation detection is often hindered in low-resource settings due to the limited availability of high-quality sequencing data, computational infrastructure, and expert annotation. These constraints are particularly problematic for key cancer-related genes such as TP53, which is frequently mutated in breast cancer and strongly associated with disease progression and treatment resistance. In recent years, deep learning approaches have shown significant promise in various genomics tasks, including variant calling, sequence classification, and gene expression analysis. Nevertheless, such models typically require large, well-annotated datasets to achieve reliable performance—a condition that is not always feasible in clinical or resource-constrained environments. Transfer learning, a machine learning technique in which knowledge learned from a large source dataset is transferred to a related target task, offers a potential solution to this limitation. It allows for the reuse of pretrained models, reducing the need for large amounts of labeled data while improving generalization. In this study, we propose and evaluate a deep learning framework for detecting TP53 mutations in breast cancer using either gene expression data or DNA sequences. We benchmark the performance of several architectures—namely, fully connected neural networks (FCNN), convolutional neural networks (CNN), bidirectional long short-term memory networks (BiLSTM), Transformers trained from scratch, and DNABERT models both trained from scratch and fine-tuned via transfer learning. All models were trained and tested on a curated subset of TCGA-BRCA samples labeled with TP53 mutation status. Our results show that DNABERT with transfer learning achieved the highest performance across all evaluation metrics, with an accuracy of 92%, F1-score of 0.90, and AUROC of 0.95. In contrast, traditional models such as FCNN and CNN using gene expression data yielded moderate performance (accuracy: 0.81–0.83), while models trained from scratch—including BiLSTM and Transformer—performed better when applied to DNA sequences (accuracy: 0.85–0.87). The consistent superiority of DNABERT highlights the value of pretrained genomic language models and transfer learning in resource-constrained scenarios. These findings underscore the promise of transformer-based models for scalable and accurate mutation detection, especially in clinical settings with limited-data availability. On the basis of our findings, we recommend adopting transfer learning approaches such as DNABERT in clinical genomics applications, integrating gene expression and sequence data to boost accuracy, and extending this framework to additional cancer-related genes to improve model generalizability.

title: Clinical accuracy and applications of large language models in pediatric orthopedics: a systematic review.
abstract:
To systematically evaluate the accuracy, reliability, and clinical applicability of artificial intelligence and large language models (LLMs) in pediatric orthopedics, comparing their performance against established clinical guidelines and assessing their utility for patient education and clinical decision support. A search of PubMed and ScienceDirect (2020-2025) identified 2624 articles using the keywords 'ChatGPT', 'Gemini', 'Claude' and 'orthopedic pediatrics'. After screening and refinement using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines, 15 studies met inclusion criteria. Studies evaluated ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Meta AI, Microsoft Copilot, and Claude across multiple pediatric orthopedic conditions across conditions like developmental dysplasia of the hip, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, and scoliosis. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q and I2 statistics, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. LLM accuracy ranged from 44.3 to 93% (pooled: 74.1%), with pooled accuracy of 74.1%. Reproducibility was moderate, with ChatGPT demonstrating a Spearman coefficient of 0.55 for complex queries. Regional expert consensus scores varied significantly (Europe: 80, North America: 65; P = 0.034; Fleiss\kappa = 0.113). Up to 33% of responses to guideline-based questions were rated neutral or inaccurate. Reading complexity was elevated (Flesch-Kincaid grade: 12.7), exceeding the recommended sixth-grade level. Parent surveys indicated 82% trust in artificial intelligence as supplementary tools with professional oversight. Minimal statistical heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 0.00%), though publication bias was detected (Egger's test P = 0.0001). LLMs show potential for education and triage but lack consistency in complex scenarios, elevated reading complexity, and significant regional variability in expert assessments. These tools should be used as educational supplements under professional medical supervision rather than for independent clinical decision-making. Broader clinical application requires domain-specific tuning, standardized evaluation, and readability optimization.


LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
Level V- systematic review.

title: Adapting teams to Human–AI collaboration: purposive programs and distinction-based task performance
abstract:
This paper develops a systems-theoretical framework for understanding how organizations can strengthen team dynamics and strategic orientation in environments increasingly shaped by Generative Artificial Intelligence. It aims to clarify how purposive programming supports effective human–AI collaboration by drawing on empirical insights from an applied educational context.
 
 
 
 The study adopts a conceptual approach grounded in Luhmann's organizational theory and is informed by practice-based workshop experiments in which student teams completed authentic tasks with and without GenAI support. The paper integrates purposive programming with distinction-based methods, systemic structural constellation formats, and the multifunctional organization concept to develop a structured orientation model for GenAI-enabled teamwork.
 
 
 
 Results show that team processes – particularly shared goals, clear roles, mutual accountability, and communication quality – exert a stronger influence on performance than GenAI access itself. High-functioning teams using GenAI produced more creative and comprehensive outputs, whereas GenAI did not compensate for weak collaboration. GenAI primarily shifts the bottleneck from production to selection and validation.
 
 
 
 The educational and practice-based setting limits generalizability of the findings. Further research should assess the transferability of purposive programming across sectors.
 
 
 
 A distinction-based four-stage pathway is proposed to support organizations in structuring GenAI-assisted teamwork through clear ends, explicit decision premises, and context-sensitive validation routines.
 
 
 
 The paper links systems theory with GenAI-enabled collaboration and provides a strategic model for managing technological complexity.

title: The Moderating Role of User Emotional Projection in the Effectiveness of AI Short-Video Marketing
abstract: With the advancement of generative artificial intelligence technology, AI short videos have assumed an increasingly important role in brand marketing. Nevertheless, users exhibit markedly different marketing responses to identical AI short videos, a variation largely moderated by their emotional projection. Drawing upon emotional communication theory and media psychological projection theory, this study employs literature integration and theoretical construction to systematically review empirical studies published between 2020 and 2026 on platforms such as Douyin, Bilibili, and YouTube. It focuses on the mechanism through which AI content characteristics—specifically the degree of anthropomorphism and the lifelikeness of narrative scenarios—influence users’ purchase intention, and further examines the moderating effect of user emotional projection within this process. The findings indicate that AI content characteristics can significantly enhance purchase intention by stimulating users’ emotional projection and parasocial interaction; however, this effect is substantially moderated by the individual’s level of emotional projection. High-emotional-projection users are more inclined to form trust-based attachment relationships, thereby strengthening marketing effectiveness, whereas low-emotional-projection users tend to activate authenticity-scrutiny mechanisms, which attenuates the persuasive impact. Moreover, the influence of emotional projection on marketing effectiveness exhibits a nonlinear threshold effect: the positive effects of content characteristics are fully realized only when emotional projection reaches a certain level. This study constructs an integrated analytical framework of “AI content characteristics → emotional projection → parasocial interaction → trust formation → purchase intention,” revealing the pivotal moderating role of users’ psychological mechanisms in AI short-video marketing and providing theoretical grounding for e-commerce content optimization in the context of intelligent communication.

title: Querying an astronomical database using large language models: the ALeRCE text-to-SQL system
abstract: We developed a text-to-structured query language (SQL) system based on large language models (LLMs) using in-context learning and applied it to the Automatic Learning for the Rapid Classification of Events (ALeRCE) astronomical database. ALeRCE is a community broker for the Zwicky Transient Facility and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The system enables users to query the database in natural language (NL) and generates executable SQL queries. To develop and evaluate the system, we constructed a set of 110 NL-SQL pairs. We propose a step-by-step generation framework comprising four modules: schema linking, query classification, prompt decomposition, and self-correction. The performance of 13 LLMs was evaluated using in-context learning and prompt engineering techniques. Text-to-SQL performance was assessed using the perfect-match (PM) rate for row identifiers (e.g., object identifiers) and column identifiers (i.e., column names). The proposed step-by-step framework consistently outperforms a direct-inference baseline, while the self-correction module consistently reduces execution errors. For Claude Opus 4.6, PM performance on row (column) identifiers is high for simple queries, reaching 0.97 (0.94), and decreases with query complexity to 0.44 (0.72) for medium queries and 0.59 (0.49) for hard queries. Among the 13 models evaluated, the best-performing LLMs for the text-to-SQL task are Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 3 Flash, and GPT-5.2-Codex.
